I need to make a decision in Monopoly.

I have $679 and am on North Carolina Avenue. I recently mortgaged New York Avenue for $100. I own Tennessee Avenue unmortgaged and New York Avenue mortgaged. Player 1 has a light blue monopoly with three houses each. Player 2 has dark blue, railroads, utilities, and several other properties.

Player 4 has $1125 and owns Mediterranean, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania Avenue. The bank holds Baltic, Virginia, St. James, Atlantic, Ventnor, Marvin Gardens, Pacific, and Short Line. I need St. James Place to complete an orange monopoly with Tennessee and New York. I can end the turn, propose a trade, mortgage Tennessee, or unmortgage New York.

Unmortgaging New York Avenue would cost $110, leaving only $569. That is below the $600 rent on Boardwalk, so I will keep it mortgaged. Mortgaging Tennessee Avenue instead would add $90 and bring cash to $769.

Mortgaging both orange properties would prevent building if I acquire St. James Place. I already have enough cash to cover Boardwalk rent, so I am now checking whether Park Place with one house is a more pressing threat.

The board spaces after North Carolina Avenue are Community Chest, Pennsylvania Avenue, Short Line, Chance, Park Place, Luxury Tax, Boardwalk, and GO. I have already rolled and landed on North Carolina.

Player 2 will act before my next roll. He has $337 and can build evenly on Boardwalk and Park Place. I will roll again on turn 44.

Player 2 needs $200 to build a second house on Park Place. That leaves $137, so he cannot afford a third house on Boardwalk before my next turn. I can survive a $500 rent on Park Place from North Carolina. I am checking whether he could mortgage something to reach three houses on Boardwalk.

Player 2 can mortgage a railroad for $100 to cover the remaining $63 needed to build three houses on Boardwalk. That would raise rent to $1400, which would bankrupt me on a roll of seven. I cannot block this during my post-turn actions. My strategic priority is acquiring St. James Place.

St. James Place costs $180, so I need to keep a reserve while surviving dark blue rent. Player 4 could acquire Pacific and complete the green monopoly; houses there cost $200 each and would be dangerous. Player 1's light blue properties with three houses are also expensive to land on.

Standard light blue house costs are $50. Player 1's three houses on each property would charge $270 on Oriental and Vermont, and $450 on Connecticut. I am safely past that side of the board.

I cannot trade for St. James Place because it is unowned. I am now considering whether any existing monopolies could be traded to help me acquire it.

I have no properties that complete another player's set. Player 1 owns all light blue properties with three houses each. Player 2 holds two of the pink properties and has Virginia unowned. Player 4 owns two of the green properties and has Pacific unowned. I own Tennessee and New York as two of the orange properties, but St. James Place is still unowned.

I am now considering a trade with player 4. I have no properties that complete another player's set right now, since St. James Place is still unowned. I could offer Tennessee Avenue or New York Avenue in exchange for cash or a better position.

I ruled out trading with player 2 or player 4 because they would not give up their dark blue properties. I am now reconsidering whether to unmortgage New York Avenue, since the $110 cost would leave me with only $569. If player 2 builds a second house on Park Place, rent would rise to $500, which I could survive with $569 remaining.

I confirmed that unmortgaging New York Avenue is fatal. With $569 after the $110 cost, a roll of seven on Boardwalk would bankrupt me. I will keep the mortgage and use the full $679 to survive the $600 rent. I am now weighing whether to mortgage Tennessee Avenue for an extra $90 buffer.

Mortgaging Tennessee Avenue would only add $90, which is insufficient to survive a three-house Boardwalk. The only lethal threat remains three houses on Boardwalk, costing $1400. Two houses on Boardwalk or Park Place are both manageable.

I will not mortgage Tennessee Avenue. That would sacrifice an unmortgaged property and still leave me vulnerable to a fully developed Boardwalk.

I am now calculating the cost of completing an orange monopoly. Three houses on each of my three properties would require $900 in construction. The resulting rent income would be substantial, but I must first land on St. James Place and then unmortgage New York Avenue.

I will not sell my orange properties. Player 1 has little cash and no interest in what I offer. Acquiring Illinois from player 2 would not complete a set for me. Player 2 holds three railroads.

Player 4 has $1125 but no board monopoly. They could buy both my orange properties and St. James Place to block me from completing orange, which would help them acquire a second monopoly while I go bankrupt. That trade is too risky unless they offer a massive return. If they gave me North Carolina and Pennsylvania Avenue instead, I would still need the unowned Pacific Place to finish a green set.

I am now reconsidering whether any trade could weaken player 2, who is the favorite to win. Player 2 holds dark blue with houses, three railroads, both utilities, and two pink properties for only $337 cash.

Player 2 has no interest in my orange properties. Player 1 is cash-poor and mortgaged, but I will not trade away my oranges for cash. I have no get-out-of-jail cards to offer. I will end the turn.

I am considering a public message to discourage player 2 from building three houses on Boardwalk. He would need $400 after mortgaging a railroad, and the chance of landing on Boardwalk is only one in six. I could mention that building there would drain his cash while leaving him exposed to threats from player 1's light blues and my potential orange monopoly.
